free_tier.stated: Linux VPS vCore 1 / RAM 2 / SSD 30 GB at USD 4.00/month: 1 Intel core shared, 2,048 MB RAM, 30 GB SSD, 10,240 GB/month bandwidth, 0.5 Gbps port, 1 IPv4, Ashburn Virginia. The tracker's line reads "starting at $4.00 per month", and the same plan at USD 4.00 is listed for Atlanta Georgia and Chicago Illinois. The vendor's FAQ states the post-quota behaviour in terms: for one and two vCPU plans the port falls to 5 Mbps.

egress.terms: 10,240 GB a month, then a port reduction to 5 Mbps on one and two vCPU plans and 10 Mbps on the rest, stated in the vendor's FAQ; no overage price is published, so the throttle is the only consequence

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: KVM with root, an IPv4 primary with extra addresses at a fee, a client-area portal and a documented API is not mentioned on the page read; ISO install is available by handing support a direct HTTP link. The company is INETCLOUD Inc.
chaining: 2 GB, 30 GB and 10 TB a month for USD 4.00 is the best balance of RAM and bytes at the monthly floor, which fits a crawler that keeps its queue in memory and writes little; once the allowance is spent the 5 Mbps throttle is a hard stop, so a crawl that might overshoot belongs on an unmetered host or on Hosting Int.

limits.value: 10,240 GB a month is 340 GB a day, then the port drops to 5 Mbps on this class of plan, which is about 54 GB a day at saturation; the drop is the harder wall and the vendor states it as policy, not as best effort.

the post-quota rule quoted: "What will happen when the bandwidth volume runs out? - For the plan with one vCPU and two vCPU, the port speed will be reduced to 5Mbps. - For all other plans, the port speed will be set to 10Mbps."

the account terms quoted: "In some instances, outbound traffic to the SMTP port may be blocked for new accounts"; "Weekly backup for free", automatic daily backups at "a 20% higher base monthly fee"; stopped instances "continue to reserve dedicated system resources (RAM, SSD storage, IP aliases, vCPU)"; "We utilize KVM virtualization on all of our infrastructure."

notes: Price is tracker-only: inet.ws/pricing answered a 404 ("Page not found"), and inet.ws/vps/ answered 200 but rendered its FAQ without the plan table, so the USD 4.00 is reported. The FAQ facts are documented and are the useful part of this record: the throttle, the SMTP block on new accounts, and the free weekly backup.
